market_pulse.note: Closed Friday at about 48,147, down 1.9%, and finished about 8% lower for the week; the index is now in correction, more than 10% below its record (AP; MarketScreener).

Closed at about 6,910, down 3.7%, a seventh straight loss and the longest losing streak since 2020; it ended in correction, more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record, and fell about 8.6% for the week (AP; MarketScreener).
Closed at about 22,618, down 5.3%, turning negative for 2026; it lost about 10% for the week, just shy of its worst week since March 2020 (AP; MarketScreener).

January WTI rose 1.2% to settle at $83.41 a barrel and the expiring December contract rose 0.9% to $83.98, but oil posted a third straight weekly loss; Brent settled at $92.57, down 3.4% for the week (Rigzone/Bloomberg).

themes.title: Chip stocks lead the rout
themes.summary: Nvidia fell about 14%, Micron about 14%, AMD about 13% and SanDisk about 16%, per MarketScreener; AP said the PHLX Semiconductor Index was down about 9% in the afternoon (MarketScreener; AP).

themes.title: S&P 500 and Dow in correction
themes.summary: Both indexes closed more than 10% below their records, the S&P 500's first correction since March 2025, and its weekly loss was the worst since April 2025 (AP; CBS News).

themes.title: Anthropic slides again
themes.summary: Anthropic shares fell 9.3% to $88.14 on their second trading day, still above the $83 IPO price, adding to doubts about returns on AI spending (AP; CBS News).

themes.title: Bond yields ease
themes.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.91% from 5.04% late Thursday, even as markets still price a near-certain Fed rate increase in December (AP; MarketScreener).

themes.title: Sentiment improves, Asia slumps
themes.summary: University of Michigan consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 in November from 48.0; earlier, Taiwan's Taiex, Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei each fell more than 5% (StockTitan; AP).

sectors.name: Technology / Semiconductors
sectors.note: Weakest area; the technology sector fund (XLK) was down about 5.4% in the afternoon, the worst of the 11 S&P sectors, led by chipmakers (Startup Fortune; MarketScreener).

sectors.name: Consumer Staples
sectors.note: Money rotated into staples; General Mills rose about 4.4%, McCormick 3.4% and Tyson Foods 2.0% (CBS News; MarketScreener).

sectors.name: Health Care
sectors.note: HCA Healthcare rose about 3.3% and UnitedHealth gained after an analyst upgrade (MarketScreener).

sectors.name: Payments / Telecom
sectors.note: Global Payments was the top S&P 500 gainer, up about 9.9%, and AT&T rose about 4.1% (MarketScreener).

watch_list.why: October PCE inflation and the second estimate of third-quarter GDP are due Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8:30 AM ET (Admirals).
U.S. markets close Thursday, Nov. 26 for Thanksgiving and close early at 1 PM ET on Friday, Nov. 27 (Admirals).
Markets price a near-certain quarter-point rate increase at the Dec. 9 Fed meeting; Fed Governor Lisa Cook said Friday that waiting longer risks falling behind (Admirals; StockTitan; MarketScreener).
